summary: Full E2E test of the FriendPlace Mini-CMS Success Stories module. BACKEND: 18/18 pytest cases pass — auth guards on every admin endpoint, CRUD (create with empty body auto-fills 'Untitled story' + status='draft' + hidden=false; GET/PATCH partial update; PATCH invalid status rejected 400; PATCH/GET on missing → 404; DELETE idempotency), the publish/draft/hidden state machine (published+visible appears on /api/public/stories, draft removed, hidden published removed, unhide restores), reorder (order field persists + /api/public/stories reflects the new ordering), and the /cms/stats.success_stories_count matches the admin list count. FRONTEND (Mission Control, Next.js website): sidebar shows the new 'Success Stories' nav item and it's clickable to /admin/success-stories; unauthenticated visits to /admin/success-stories and /admin/success-stories/{id} redirect to /admin/login (verified); empty-state '📖 No stories yet' renders; '+ New story' creates a draft and routes to the editor; editor allows filling title, TipTap body, author name/role/location; 👁️ Preview modal opens and renders the story using the same StoryCard component as the public page (visual parity confirmed via screenshot); 🚀 Publish moves the story to status=published, hides that button, exposes 'Move to draft', and the story becomes immediately visible on /api/public/stories; 'Move to draft' removes it from the public feed; Delete button removes the row from the list and the DB; Dashboard 'Success stories' summary tile renders and the 'Add Success Story' Quick Action navigates via ?new=1 which auto-creates a draft and drops the admin straight into the editor. IMPORTANT INFRA FINDING: on the preview URL, /success-stories is routed to the Expo mobile app (not to the Next.js marketing page at /app/website/app/success-stories/page.tsx), so the shared <StoryCard>-based public grid + '🦋 The first stories are being written.' empty state cannot be exercised through the emergent preview — nginx routes only /admin, /_next and /api/uploads to the Next.js website. Non-blocking for prod (site lives on its own hostname there) but Garry cannot preview the public page in this environment. Cleanup: every cms_success_stories row created during testing was deleted (Mongo count = 0, /api/public/stories returns []). Admin password NOT touched — used _make_admin_token() to mint a JWT for the existing 'hello@friendplace.com.au' admin.

minor.issue: New draft auto-appends order = <count of existing docs>. If a story is later deleted from the middle, subsequent creates can collide with an existing order value (multiple rows sharing the same order). The /reorder endpoint fixes it, but the initial list sort ('order' asc, 'created_at' desc) will produce a stable ordering only because of the tie-break. Not a bug today, but consider using max(order)+1 or resequencing after delete.
created_by is stored as admin['email'] but never returned to the client type (SuccessStory) — harmless but adds a stray field on GETs. Not blocking.

integration_issues.flow: Public marketing page /success-stories on the emergent preview
integration_issues.issue: Nginx (/app/config/nginx/app-proxy.conf) routes only /admin, /_next, and /api/uploads to the Next.js website (port 3001). Every other frontend path — including /success-stories — falls through to the Expo mobile app on port 3002. Result: visiting https://<preview>/success-stories serves the Expo web build (title 'FriendPlace' + expo-router bundle), not the Next.js 'Real people. Real belonging.' page with the shared <StoryCard>. So the item-12 empty state and the grid rendering can only be verified in production or by running the website dev server directly on :3001. The /api/public/stories endpoint itself is correct and returns the expected filtered payload.

issues: TipTap emits a startup warning: `[tiptap warn]: Duplicate extension names found: ['link']`. Not visible to users but adds noise to the console and can lead to subtle link-mark bugs when a starter kit already provides Link and the code adds it again. Consider removing the extra Link.configure() or disabling StarterKit's link.

Editor has NO explicit testID attributes on the header buttons (Preview, Save draft, Publish, Move to draft, Hide) or on the form inputs. Selectors have to fall back to text-content matching, which works in English only. Adding data-testid values would harden future automated testing.
Row actions (↑, ↓, Edit, Delete) don't have data-testid; automated tests must rely on class .cms-btn-danger and button text. Fine for now but flag for future.

action_items: Optional: add data-testid attributes to the admin editor buttons (preview-btn, publish-btn, move-to-draft-btn, save-draft-btn, hide-btn) and the list row actions so future test agents don't have to depend on emoji-prefixed button text.
Optional: dedupe the TipTap Link extension so the console warning disappears (`Duplicate extension names found: ['link']`).

Consider re-sequencing `order` on delete (or using max(order)+1 on create) to avoid duplicate order values after mid-list deletions. Not user-visible today because /reorder repairs it, but a latent hazard.

Environment/nginx note only: if you want Garry to eyeball the public /success-stories page in the emergent preview, add a location rule mapping /success-stories → website_upstream in /app/config/nginx/app-proxy.conf. Prod deployment (Vercel) is unaffected.
critical_code_review_comments: cms_module.py list_stories / _load_stories don't strip the `created_by` field before returning to admin/public — leaks the admin's email address to the public /api/public/stories response. Low sensitivity (email is already on the About page) but worth stripping for tidiness.
Editor page relies on the ProseMirror div for the TipTap body — no testID/data-testid, so keyboard-only or programmatic value setting is fragile.

PreviewModal in /app/website/app/admin/success-stories/[id]/page.tsx uses the current in-memory story state, so if the admin hasn't clicked Save, they may preview stale/newer content depending on when they opened the modal. That's actually the DESIRED behaviour (Preview shows what's on screen), but it means Preview does NOT round-trip through the DB — worth documenting so testers don't expect DB-truth.

The public /success-stories Next.js page fetches with `next.revalidate = 60`. In production this caches for 60s so newly-published stories can be up to a minute stale. Acceptable, but the review request implies immediate freshness — flag to Garry.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 12 admin/dashboard flows I could exercise via the preview URL — the 13th (public marketing page rendering) is unreachable via the preview due to nginx routing (see integration_issues).

seed_data_creation: During testing, 5 cms_success_stories rows were created (pytest fixture + Playwright flows). ALL of them were deleted on teardown — verified via GET /api/cms/success-stories (count=0) and GET /api/public/stories (stories=[]). Garry starts with an empty list. Admin account 'hello@friendplace.com.au' was NOT touched (no password change, no delete) — a JWT was minted via cms_module._make_admin_token() for testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite: `MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017 DB_NAME=test_database JWT_SECRET=$(grep JWT_SECRET /app/backend/.env|cut -d= -f2) pytest /app/backend/tests/test_success_stories.py -v`. The suite mints a JWT for the pre-existing admin (no password required) and wipes every cms_success_stories row on teardown, so it's safe to re-run repeatedly. For frontend testing, inject the localStorage keys `fp_cms_token` (a valid JWT) and `fp_cms_admin` (JSON `{id,email,display_name}`) BEFORE navigating to any /admin route — no login page interaction needed. Reminder: /success-stories on the preview URL is served by the Expo mobile app, NOT the Next.js website — verify public rendering either by hitting the website dev server on port 3001 directly, or via the /api/public/stories JSON payload.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs found in the Success Stories module. The only real environmental gap is nginx routing (see integration_issues) which is a preview-environment concern, not a code bug.
